title: A pending PATH2 IMAGE after DIRECT must not swallow VIFcodes
problem: When a DIRECT ends with an IMAGE GIFtag whose data arrives later, upstream treats the next raw bytes as pixel data (m_vif1PendingPath2ImageQwc branch, lines 307-330). Those bytes are actually MARK/DIRECT VIFcodes, so the upload shifts by 8 bytes (garbled fonts and CLUTs).
approach: Always parse VIFcodes; wrap only the next DIRECT's payload in a synthesized IMAGE tag. Raw continuation is kept only for a DIRECT truncated at the end of a DMA buffer.
scope_evidence: general; KZ says it verified byte-for-byte against PCSX2 EE RAM via PINE. The upstream code matches the bug pattern they describe.

title: paraLLEl-GS renderer with an ordering contract, mailbox presentation and a threaded CPU backend
problem: Need a GPU GS, an asynchronous renderer and correct readbacks.
approach: (a) The GSRasterBackend contract is documented: calls are ordered from a single producer; ReadVram, SnapshotVram, ConsumeLocalToHost and Sync(LocalToHost) observe all earlier calls. New virtuals: PresentToMailbox, ResetPresentation, Kick, WaitFlipBacklog, VerifyPages, Shutdown. (b) GSGpuRenderer is Vulkan-free and takes raw input gif(path,data,bytes), reg(addr,val), present(privRegs[15], vsyncTick, flip), snapshotVram, readTransfer; frames come back through a lock-free triple-buffer mailbox (optionally a shared Vulkan image). (c) GSGpuBackend is a null GSRasterBackend that answers reads from the GPU. (d) Modes VENDETTA_GS=gpu|cpu|both, plus VERIFY, which compares GS memory page CRCs between the two renderers.

problem: Codegen bugs (like the ones above) are hard to find.
